verdict: The Kinetic Chaos is MedKayfab at its sharpest: 56 cards spanning fractures, fixation, arthroplasty, infection, pharmacology and bone tumours, each giving a wrestling character name to a clinical fact that medical students traditionally forget. Fat-Embolism-Felix on motorcycles, Silent-Swiss-Cheese Pam, and Granny-Snap Hilda do more mnemonic work per square centimetre than most textbook diagrams. The synthesis quest cards on the final page add a clever exam layer. Only structural weakness: cards 09–12 on page 4 lack printed card numbers, and the Cauda-Equina-Caleb Redux may confuse first-timers without a cross-reference tag. Table-ready: Yes.
blurb: Fifty-six bone-and-knife wrestlers teach orthopaedic surgery through chaos — from Granny-Snap Hilda to Midnight-Numb Carl, every clinical crisis becomes a character you will never forget. Essential for med students, surgical residents, and anyone who has ever broken a bone.

coverQA.coverNote: One of the strongest MedKayfab covers — the welding mask on FrizzleBob is a perfect ortho-surgeon metaphor, and the rat yelling 'more torque' at a hip X-ray is an instant meme. The Neo-Humerus Prototype blueprints reward close inspection.

notes: 15 pages: 1 cover + 14 card spreads, 4 cards per spread in 2x2 grid. Cards 01-08 visible numbered on pages 2-3; cards 09-12 on page 4 lack printed card numbers (layout gap). Cards 13-52 numbered sequentially. Page 15 holds 4 special cards: The Orthopaedic Attending (Boss / Doc FrizzleBob, no POWER or LORE text printed) and Synthesis Quests 1-3 (patient-case learning cards). Cauda-Equina-Caleb appears twice: card 09 (Nerve Squash, saddle anaesthesia) and card 35 (Redux, perianal numbness/sciatica) — intentional dual-presentation teaching design. STAT boxes function as quick-reference clinical pearls in card corners; no RAF dice system on this deck. Page 10 uses a darker red-splatter border signalling emergency/high-acuity theme. Stay fluffy! is the recurring deck catchphrase.
